text: Withania somnifera (Ashwagandha) — King of Ayurvedic herbs. IP considerations: Extensive prior art in classical texts (Charaka Samhita). Active compounds: withanolides (withaferin A, withanolide D). Patentable aspects: novel extraction methods, standardized extracts with specific withanolide profiles, novel delivery systems (nano, liposomal), combinations with synergistic herbs. Major patent holders: Natreon, Ixoreal, universities. FTO needed for commercial products. Key markets: stress, energy, sports nutrition.

Curcuma longa (Turmeric/Haldi) — Golden spice with extensive IP activity. Prior art: wound healing (famously challenged US patent), culinary use, traditional medicine. Active: curcuminoids (curcumin, demethoxycurcumin, bisdemethoxycurcumin). Challenge: poor bioavailability. Patentable: enhanced bioavailability formulations (piperine combinations, phytosomes, nanoparticles, BCM-95, C3 Complex), novel extraction, specific therapeutic applications with clinical data. Caution: many composition patents invalidated for obviousness or prior art.

Bacopa monnieri (Brahmi) — Memory enhancing herb. Prior art: extensive Ayurvedic literature for cognitive enhancement. Active compounds: bacosides (bacoside A, bacopaside). Patentable aspects: standardized extracts (Bacognize, KeenMind, Synapsa with specific bacoside profiles), novel extraction preserving bacoside ratio, combinations for cognitive health, extended-release formulations. Market: nootropics, cognitive health supplements. Ensure clinical data supports cognitive claims for regulatory and IP purposes.

Ocimum sanctum/tenuiflorum (Tulsi/Holy Basil) — Adaptogenic and immunomodulatory herb. Prior art: religious and medicinal use documented extensively. Active compounds: eugenol, ursolic acid, rosmarinic acid, ocimumosides. Patentable: specific extract combinations (OciBest, Holixer), novel uses with clinical validation, extraction methods, formulations targeting specific health benefits. Note: tulsi is widely cultivated and traded; distinguish patentable innovations from commodity products.

Azadirachta indica (Neem) — Famous biopiracy case subject. Prior art: extensive traditional use documented in TKDL and literature. Active: azadirachtin, nimbin, nimbidin. Patentable aspects: purified compounds with novel processes, pest control formulations beyond traditional knowledge, novel pharmaceutical/cosmetic applications with supporting data. Caution: any neem-based patent will face Section 3(p) scrutiny; must clearly differentiate from prior TK. Document the novel technical contribution meticulously.

Asparagus racemosus (Shatavari) — Women's health and adaptogen herb. Prior art: Charaka Samhita, classical formulations. Active compounds: saponins (shatavarins). Patentable: standardized extracts with specific saponin content, combinations for reproductive health, hormone modulation formulations, novel delivery systems for saponins. Market: women's health, lactation support, menopause. Ensure clinical studies support health claims for differentiated IP position.

Tinospora cordifolia (Giloy/Guduchi) — Immunomodulatory herb. Prior art: Rasayana category in classical texts. Active: berberine, tinosporin, giloin. Patent considerations: Gained attention during COVID-19; many recent patent filings. Patentable: novel immunomodulatory formulations with clinical data, standardized extracts, combinations for specific immune conditions. Caution: traditional immunomodulatory use is well documented; need to show novel technical contribution beyond TK.

Phyllanthus emblica (Amla/Indian Gooseberry) — Highest natural Vitamin C. Prior art: Triphala component, hair/skin care, Chyawanprash ingredient. Active: emblicanin A/B, gallic acid, ellagic acid, vitamin C. Patentable: stabilized vitamin C extracts, specific antioxidant standardization, novel formulations beyond traditional use, combinations with other fruits for enhanced effect. Widely used in cosmetics and nutraceuticals; large IP landscape.

Commiphora wightii (Guggul) — Cholesterol and joint health. Prior art: Guggulsterone compounds known, Ayurvedic use documented. Challenge: plant over-harvested, sustainability concerns, CITES-like restrictions in some regions. Patentable: sustainable extraction methods, purified guggulsterones with specific ratios, combinations for metabolic syndrome, novel delivery overcoming stability issues. Note: sourcing sustainability may affect commercialization — document sustainable supply chain.

Triphala (combination of Haritaki, Bibhitaki, Amalaki) — Classical Ayurvedic formulation. Prior art: extensively documented in classical texts, FDA GRAS status. Traditional ratios known. Patentable: novel ratios with unexpected benefits (clinical data needed), enhanced bioavailability formulations, specific therapeutic applications with supporting studies, synergy with additional components. Caution: traditional Triphala cannot be patented; innovations must go beyond classical formula.

Zingiber officinale (Ginger/Adrak) — Culinary and medicinal spice. Prior art: extensive food and medicinal use globally. Active: gingerols, shogaols. Challenge: widely known, hard to patent basic applications. Patentable: novel extraction yielding enhanced gingerol content, specific therapeutic applications with clinical evidence (nausea, inflammation), combinations with other herbs showing synergy, novel delivery systems. Being commodity traded, FTO landscape is complex.

Piper nigrum (Black Pepper/Kali Mirch) — Bioavailability enhancer. Key compound: piperine. Famous patent: Sabinsa's BioPerine for bioenhancement. Prior art: traditional use with medicines (Trikatu). Patentable: piperine standardized extracts, novel bioenhancement combinations (already extensively patented by Sabinsa), alternative bioenhancers. Caution: Sabinsa has enforced BioPerine patents; FTO check essential for piperine-containing products marketed as bioenhancers.

Saraca asoca (Ashoka) — Women's health herb. Prior art: classical use for menstrual disorders. Active: catechins, tannins, saponins. Conservation: listed as vulnerable due to over-harvesting. Patentable: sustainable cultivation methods, standardized extracts, combinations for women's health with clinical validation. Note: source authentication important — often adulterated with Polyalthia longifolia. Document sourcing and authentication for quality and IP purposes.

Moringa oleifera (Drumstick Tree/Sahjan) — Nutritional powerhouse. Prior art: traditional food and medicine use documented. Active: isothiocyanates, phenolics, proteins. Growing interest: superfood category, nutritional supplements. Patentable: novel processing methods preserving nutrients, specific health applications with clinical evidence, formulations for malnutrition intervention, water purification applications. Large commodity market; differentiate through quality standardization and clinical validation.

IP strategy for common AYUSH herbs: 1) Accept that traditional uses are prior art — focus on novel innovations. 2) Differentiate through: novel extraction, specific standardization, enhanced bioavailability, clinical evidence for new applications. 3) Conduct thorough prior art search including TKDL. 4) Build clinical evidence supporting novel claims. 5) Consider process patents when composition patents are blocked. 6) Combine with trademark and trade secret protection. 7) FTO analysis before commercialization — crowded landscape for popular herbs.
